text: Describe the duty owed to a trespasser under the Occupiers’ Liability Act 1984.
Assess the fairness of the duty in relation to both the occupier and trespasser. [25]
In the tort of negligence, losses of a purely economic nature should be treated very differently
from personal injury and damage to property.
Describe the rules governing pure economic loss. Assess the validity of the statement above. [25]
Describe the purpose of the remedy of damages in relation to the tort of negligence. Assess the
extent to which the current rules achieve justice for the claimant. [25]
Section B
Jim is late for work and driving at speed when his car collides with a taxi, driven by Shannon. She
is not wearing a seatbelt and is seriously injured. Jim is trapped in his car.
Emma is a self-employed hairdresser. Although Emma does not witness the accident, it happens
outside her shop. She calls the emergency services and stays with Jim until they arrive. She is
very distressed as the injuries of both Shannon and Jim appear to be life threatening.
Shannon and Jim are taken to hospital and following treatment both make a full recovery.
Since the incident, Emma has been unable to work due to anxiety and stress. She eventually has
no choice but to close her business.
Advise the parties as to their rights, responsibilities and remedies in relation to negligence. [25]
Flynn drives to Barchester shopping centre. He parks his car in a very narrow space in the car
park. On his return to his car he finds Bob waiting for him.
Bob is the owner of the car next to Flynn’s. He has been unable to get into his car as Flynn has
parked too close to the driver’s side of Bob’s car. Bob is very angry, raises his fists and shouts at
Flynn to move his car immediately.
Flynn tells Bob to calm down and that he should have used another door to enter the car. After
further argument Flynn gets into his car and begins to drive away. Bob has called the police and
he stands in front of Flynn’s car. Flynn continues to drive away even though Bob jumps on to
the front of the car. Flynn speeds up and Bob falls from the car, sustaining a broken arm and
concussion.
Advise the parties as to their rights and responsibilities in relation to trespass to the person. [25]
Anya has recently moved back to her family home as she is saving to buy her own property. Her
mother Monica is the owner of the property and she does not charge Anya for rent or bills. Anya
has a dog which barks frequently both during the day and at night. The neighbour, Sam, has
complained about this, but Monica says that there is nothing she can do about the dog.
Sam is a nurse and he often works at night and sleeps during the day. Anya is angry about the fact
that Sam has complained about her dog. She has now started to play very loud music as soon as
she sees Sam returning from a night shift. Consequently, Sam is unable to sleep. Monica is not
aware of what Anya is doing as she works during the day.
Advise the parties as to their rights, responsibilities and remedies in relation to private nuisance.
